card.line: Succoth means "shelters." It was a place east of the Jordan where Jacob settled, and it was also the Israelites' first camp after leaving Egypt.

moments.title: Jacob builds a home
moments.text: After Esau went back to Seir, Jacob went on to Succoth. There he built a house for himself and shelters for his livestock, and that is how the place got its name.

moments.title: First camp after Egypt
moments.text: The Israelites traveled from Rameses to Succoth with about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children. Then they set out from Succoth and camped at Etham.

moments.title: A stop on the journey
moments.text: The list of camps in the wilderness says the Israelites camped at Succoth and then set out for Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.

moments.title: Land for the Gadites
moments.text: Succoth was named among the cities in the valley east of the Jordan. It was part of the land that went to the clans of the Gadites.

moments.title: Gideon is refused bread
moments.text: Gideon asked the men of Succoth for bread for his worn-out troops. The leaders refused. Later Gideon came back and disciplined the men of Succoth with thorns and briers.

moments.title: Bronze cast for the temple
moments.text: The king had the bronze articles for the house of the LORD cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan, between Succoth and Zarethan.
